content.title: About
content.content: Pickled fish is fish that has been cured in a brine made of salt, vinegar, spices and sometimes sugar. The pickling process preserves the fish, gives it a distinctive tangy‑salty flavor and extends its shelf life. Commonly used species include herring, mackerel, cod or salmon.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pickling fish has been practiced since ancient times as a method of food preservation.
Each country has its own traditional recipes: Russian pickled herring, Japanese “sake‑tsuba”, Swedish “surströmming”.
The acidic brine helps destroy microbial cells, making the product safer.
Pickled fish is often served as a snack with beer or as part of salads.
Omega‑3 fatty acids remain in pickled fish, although some may be lost during long storage.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Fish provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Pickled fish retains EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Fish contains B12, B6 and niacin, important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It is a source of selenium, iodine and phosphorus, beneficial for thyroid function and bones.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Pickled fish contains virtually no carbs, making it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The large amount of salt can be problematic for people with hypertension or kidney disease.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Improper pickling or storage can allow growth of pathogens such as Listeria.

items.title: Histamine formation
items.content: During prolonged storage histamine may accumulate, causing food intolerance.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pickled fish can be enjoyed as a snack, added to salads, sandwiches, pastas, or used in hot dishes like casseroles. Before serving, drain excess brine.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep pickled fish refrigerated at 0‑4 °C in its original brine in an airtight container. For longer storage (over 2‑3 weeks) change the brine periodically. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
